newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Australia pushes for new warship deal with Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: Australia pushes for new warship deal with Kuwait.

text.p: Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer on Saturday lobbied for an Australian company bidding for a contract in Kuwait for helicopter-carrying missile vessels.
"I emphasised the competitive strengths of Australia's defence industry, particularly in naval vessel construction," Fischer, a deputy premier, told a news conference after talks in Kuwait.
The Australian privately-held Transfield has presented Kuwait with a warship proposal to meet the naval requirements, with various arming options.
"Yes we discused this," said Fischer, expressing hope the Australian firm would be "an effective tenderer in the final stages" of the competition.

Transfield Director Robert Salteri later told Reuters his firm had carried out tank tests on its 85-metre (280 feet), 1,600-tonne vessel on offer which is capable of carrying various American and European missile systems.
Several firms from Europe and the United States are also bidding for the three-year-old contract which industry sources said was not in an advanced stage.

"I think this contract is a couple of years off," said Salteri whose company in 1993 completed delivery to Kuwait of four 40- metre (132 feet), 500-tonne coast guard vessels ordered prior to the 1991 Gulf War to free Kuwait from Iraqi occupation.
Fischer will next week represent Australia at Abu Dhabi's international arms exhibition but Transfield will not take part in these competitions.
Fischer will also visit Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, and Saudi Arabia -- the world's largest barley importer -- as part of Australia's efforts to be a key food supplier to Middle Eastern states.

He said the resumption of wheat, barley and rice exports led to the doubling in the value of Australia's exports to Kuwait, rising to $127 million in 1996 from $66 million the previous year. Australia's imports from Kuwait in 1996 were worth $91 million and $67 million in 1995, Fischer added.
The two sides also discussed possible direct air links.

"Another area yet to develop and hopefully we will soon (develop) is a direct aviation link...We have negotiated on this and it is under consideration," Fischer said. "We need these air links if we are really going to put further depth into the two-way trade, investment and tourism."
